title: Widgets get smaller every time they're moved between screens
line: Desktop widgets keep their size when dragged to another screen instead of shrinking with every move.
explanation: When a widget is dropped on another screen's desktop, AppletsLayout::createContainerForApplet builds a new container sized from the applet's current size plus the container's padding. That size was set between beginCreate() and completeCreate() of the QML container, before the padding bindings (the frame margins, 16 px a side) were evaluated, so the padding counted as zero; once the bindings applied, the content lost 2x16 px. The change sets the position and size after completeCreate(), so the padding is really added and the content keeps its size.

commits.message:
containmentlayoutmanager: add container padding after its bindings are set

A widget moved to another screen got a container sized from its applet
before the container's padding bindings were evaluated, so the padding
counted as zero and the widget lost it on every move. Size it after that.

BUG: 522198

media.caption: Master: a Calculator (228x356) after three moves between screens is 132x260 and its buttons are squeezed
With the fix: the same three moves, the Calculator is still 260x372

review.text: Identifies and fixes the exact root cause in plasma-workspace's AppletsLayout::createContainerForApplet: container padding was read before m_appletContainerComponent->completeCreate() evaluated the QML padding bindings, causing widgets moved across screens to lose 32 px of frame padding on every transfer. Moving the position and size calculation after completeCreate() cleanly preserves widget sizes across multi-screen moves, and the minor side effect of newly created widgets starting with their true content size plus padding is well documented and desirable.

reviews.text: Identifies and fixes the exact root cause in plasma-workspace's AppletsLayout::createContainerForApplet: container padding was read before m_appletContainerComponent->completeCreate() evaluated the QML padding bindings, causing widgets moved across screens to lose 32 px of frame padding on every transfer. Moving the position and size calculation after completeCreate() cleanly preserves widget sizes across multi-screen moves, and the minor side effect of newly created widgets starting with their true content size plus padding is well documented and desirable.

Correct root cause in the right place: createContainerForApplet() read the container's padding between beginCreate() and completeCreate(), when the QML padding bindings aren't evaluated yet (the existing NOTE comment even says so), so every cross-screen recreate dropped 2x16 px. Moving the position/size code after completeCreate() is minimal, keeps the saved-geometry and initialSize paths intact, and the rig numbers (three moves at a constant size, Battery round-trip, restart persistence) back it up. The one visible side effect, newly added widgets that already have an applet size getting the frame on top (about 32 px larger than on master), is the original code's evident intent and is documented; it would be worth one sentence in the commit message so reviewers aren't surprised.
